blocks.s: A tool is one file that says what questions to make. Everything else (the three modes, the buttons, printing, links, the pictures that build up) is done by a shared shell, so the tool file only holds the maths.

items: You (or a spec in `specs/`) say what the tool should teach.
The tool file turns that into questions and worked answers.
One line in `src/registry.ts` puts it on the site. Nothing else needs editing to add a route or a landing-page card.
The shell (`src/shared/ToolShell.tsx`, with its body in `ToolShellCore.tsx`) wraps the tool and gives it Whiteboard, Worked Example, Worksheet, printing, share links and the rest.
Tests check every tool automatically.
A script reads the code and writes the facts the dashboard shows. You never type those.

guide.title: What is inside a tool file

blocks.s: A tool lives in `src/tools/<Strand>/<Name>.tsx`. In order, a tool file holds:

head: Part
What it is
Be aware
rows: Types
The small shapes the tool uses for its own numbers
Local to the file. Do not redefine shared types
`TOOL_CONFIG`

The tabs (sub-tools), the levels, and the Question Options (the switches a teacher can tick; mark one `displayOnly` if it only changes how the same question is shown; the heading over each pool is Title Case and uses the site's one wording: "Method", "Working Shown", "Answer Format", "Ask for")
Options that are alternatives belong in one pool; switches that can stack are separate. See "Question Options" in `CLAUDE.md`
`<Tool>.about.ts`

The plain-language words: what the tool is for, what each sub-tool is for, one short plain line per level, and one sentence for every Question Option saying what it is for. They feed "About this tool", the level (i) and the hover note on each option
Short and plain, no jargon; a test checks they exist and that no option is left unexplained
`generateQuestion`
Makes one question: the display, the answer and the worked steps
Must give every question a `key` that describes it (never just a random number) so a worksheet does not repeat
`export const __test`
Hands the config and generator to the automatic tests
Never delete it. The build fails if a shell tool lacks it
`export default function App()`
Renders `<ToolShell … />`
Leave as the template has it

guide.title: What the shell does for you

blocks.s: Whiteboard, Worked Example (step by step, with the line building up one mark at a time), Worksheet (columns, differentiated levels, fullscreen), PDF printing, the level buttons, Question Options popovers, "About this tool", share links, Printables in the burger menu, recent and pinned questions, the ink pen on every page, and Teach / Lessons / Depth when a tool supplies them. A tool never writes its own buttons, popovers, print window or link handling.

head: File or folder
What it is for
Be aware
rows: `src/registry.ts`
The one list of every tool: id, path, name, description, strand, whether it is live

`enabled: false` means in development (only shows with Developing tools on). Never edit `App.tsx` or the landing page to add a tool. A tool's `id` is its route without the slash (a test checks it) and is also the key of its dashboard note, so renaming one means copying the note; if a route changes, list the old address under `aliases` and it redirects. A strand's `subject` places it on a landing-page tab (`All subjects` shows it under every tab)
`src/shared/ToolShell.tsx` + `ToolShellCore.tsx`
The shell for question generators

`ToolShell.tsx` is the small lessons wrapper; `ToolShellCore.tsx` (about 990 lines) holds the state and picks the screen. The screens (Whiteboard, Worked Example, Worksheet, phone layout) are components in `components/`, and the share-link, option, saved-setup, worksheet-generation and question-lifecycle logic are small files beside it (`shellUrl`, `shellOptions`, `shellPersist`, `worksheetGenerate`, `questionLifecycle`, `useWorksheetFit`, `useVisualiser`); each screen runs behind a failure guard that names it (`shellDiagnostics`, `ShellPartBoundary`), `npm run lint` checks the React hooks rules, and `npm run smoke:shell` opens every screen in a browser to check (both run in CI)
`src/shared/index.ts`
The barrel: the one door tools import through
Tools import from `../../shared` only. Several tools still reach around it (a recorded decision)
`src/shared/types.ts`
Shared shapes: questions, steps, config, options
`src/shared/questionExtras.ts`
The private hand-over between a tool and the shell: every underscore field on a question (`_diagram`, `_rawValues`, `_stagedReveal`, `_printText`…) is listed once, with a typed reader `extras(q)`
Add a new field here first; a test fails on a field it does not list, on a listed one nothing uses, and on `(q as any)._x`
`src/shared/printables.ts`
Ready-made A4 sheets with no questions (blank number lines, place value tables, ratio tables, coordinate grids) and the one print path for them

A tool passes `printables` and the burger menu lists them; only offer one when the working is built on a blank the student fills in (a test checks it). A new sheet is a new function here, never a print routine in a tool
`src/shared/helpers.ts`
Everyday generator helpers: `randInt`, `pick`, `step`, `mStep`, `tStep`, `fracStr`, `pickActive`, `fmt`
`mStep` is the default way to write a working step. Never put `\text{}` inside a step
`src/shared/math.ts`
Shared number maths: `gcd`, `lcm`, `gcdAll`, `shuffle`
`gcd` is never negative; `lcm` is 0 if either number is 0; `shuffle` is fair and returns a new list. Use these, do not write local copies. More helpers are listed as decisions
`src/shared/prompts.ts`
Says a shared prompt ("Simplify:") once on a worksheet
A question shaped as a maths-free line then a maths-only line gets this for free
`src/shared/print.ts`, `printDiagram.ts`, `worksheetLayout.ts`
Printing: text sheets, picture sheets, and the page-fill engine both share
Picture tools pass `handleDiagramPrint` and never hand-roll a print grid
`src/shared/layoutMode.ts`
Decides phone, tablet or laptop layout, including the "View as" override
Never read `matchMedia` yourself; use `useLayoutMode()`
`src/shared/placeValue.ts`, `ratioTable.ts`, `counters.ts`, `sigFigs.ts`, `carry.ts`, `longDivision.ts`
The pictures (representations) and their data
Pick one of the eight core pictures before inventing a new one
`src/shared/components/`
The shared screens and widgets (question display, popovers, tables, Depth stage, ink pen)
Tools use these through the barrel
`src/shared/depth.ts`, `lessons.ts`, `TeachingDeck.tsx`
Depth questions, lessons, and Teach slide decks
Optional extras a tool opts into
`src/shared/calibration.ts`
Measures how hard questions are so worksheets run easy to hard
Re-run the calibration after any change to a calibrated generator
`src/shared/decision/`, `src/shared/cs/`
The two other shells (Decision Maths; Computer Science revision)
Separate by design; they do not use `ToolShell`
`src/tests/`
The automatic checks
`generators.test.ts` renders every maths string for every tool; `organisation.test.ts` fails if a tool is unregistered or uncategorised
`src/generated/toolFacts.json`
The facts the dashboard shows, read from the code
Never edit by hand. Run `npm run facts` after changing a tool or the registry, and commit the result
`src/admin/`
The dashboard itself
Reads the generated facts and the notes
`api/`
The small server piece that stores the dashboard notes
Cannot import from `src/`
`specs/`
Briefs: what to build, with the sample answers that define correct
Only briefs marked `Status: ready` are built; mark `implemented` when done
`scripts/`
`new-tool` (scaffolds a tool), `toolFacts` (the facts), `notesPages` (planner pages), `adminDocs` (these dashboard pages)
Run through `npm run …`
`docs/`
The written project: plan, tidy-up list, history, glossary, design notes
See the documentation map in `CLAUDE.md`
`CLAUDE.md`
The rules Claude reads every session
The single source of truth for conventions

guide.title: Extra files that sit beside a tool

blocks.s: A bigger tool can have helper files next to it, named after it:

items: `<Tool>Depth.ts` holds the Depth questions (for example `OrderOfOperationsDepth.ts`).
`<Tool>Lessons.ts` holds the lesson steps; `<Tool>Teach.ts` holds the Teach slides.
`<Tool>.calibration.ts` holds the measured difficulty table. It is written by a test run, not by hand.
Large tools split their maths into `…Core.ts`, `…Algebra.ts` and so on (Indices does this).
**Mark:** Decide (two tools left; File Sizes and the Decision tools are settled, see below)

**What we found:** Six question tools were not live. **File Sizes went live 2026-10-26.** **Travelling Salesperson, Route Inspection and Mixed Strategies** (Decision) are no longer loose: they join the Decision exam-style questions prong (`docs/PROJECTS.md`), which takes each to go-live as it gets exam chains like Critical Path Analysis and Network Flows. Two remain: **Simplifying Ratios** (the oldest form: no question options) and **Perimeter** (over a year old, the most outdated). Another 14 internal pages (the Tool Shell template, the Technique and Skill libraries, 11 technique previews) sit in the registry as workshop pages.
**Why it matters:** Unfinished tools clutter the registry and the counts.

**Suggested move:** *Simplifying Ratios:* list the Question Options it could gain, then fold it into a separate ratio tool rather than keep a stand-alone (which tool is still to choose: Fraction to Ratio and Ratio Sharing are the neighbours). *Perimeter:* rework it to the current standard (it predates most of the shell), starting from a short brief of what it should teach.
**To decide:** Which tool Simplifying Ratios joins and what its options are; what the reworked Perimeter covers (compound shapes, missing sides, arcs).
**Leaning:** Merge Simplifying Ratios into the neighbour whose sub-tools it overlaps most, once its options are listed; write the Perimeter brief before touching code.

plan.title: 2. Built, but only on a handful of tools

items: **Mark:** Decide

**What we found:** Depth banks: 4 of 42 ToolShell tools. Lessons: 2 tools (Indices, Rounding), Developing-tools only. Teach decks: 3 tools, Developing-tools only. Calibrated worksheets: 1 tool (Order of Operations). Techniques engine: a few tools, plus 11 preview pages. Developing picture in Worked Example: 22 tools, with 19 live tools having none. Printable sheets: 1 tool (Rounding).
**Why it matters:** Strong features that most teachers never meet look like gaps in the site.
**Suggested move:** Grow each one tool by tool as part of that tool's review, or decide a few stay a premium extra.
**To decide:** Which capabilities get rolled out widely and which stay as extras.
**Leaning:** Grow the developing picture gradually; decide the rest per capability.
**Mark:** Finish

**What we found:** Median is 4 options per level, but Rounding (20), Ordering Numbers (18), Binomial Expansion (15), File Sizes (15), Speed/Distance/Time (14) and Order of Operations (13) are walls. The groups already sort into what is asked, the numbers, notation, method, the answer and support.
**Why it matters:** A teacher faced with twenty switches cannot find the one they want.
**Suggested move:** Regroup tool by tool into those six groups (the layered popover is parked, see item 5), after the structural items above.
**To decide:** Whether to cap options per level.
**Leaning:** Group first, cap later.
**Mark:** Fold

**What we found:** `AlgebraTiles` 2,039 lines, `SystemArchitecture` 1,713, `OrderOfOperations` 1,597, `Surds` 1,197, `FunctionalSkillsGenerator` 2,228, plus `TeachingDeck` 1,244 and `WorksheetBuilder` 823 in the shell.
**Why it matters:** They are slow to read and to change safely.
**Suggested move:** Split on the seams that already exist (generator, question renderer, Depth, teach), only when a file is touched.
**To decide:** Which to split and on what seams.
**Leaning:** Not urgent.
**Mark:** Decide

**What we found:** Colour schemes (a long-term accessibility update that needs a proper rework first) · Complexity stepper · slide-strip lesson builder and slide templates · saved lessons · `.pptx` export · layered Question Options popover (the six groups in item 3) · skill drill-downs: the `[[skill|term]]` markers stay in three tools, inert until the Skill Library is un-parked (`docs/BACKBENCH.md`), and the smoke tests still check each marker names a real skill.
**Why it matters:** They are kept so they are not lost, not because they are scheduled.
**Suggested move:** Pick one back up only when a current item clears.
**To decide:** Which idea, if any, comes next.
**Leaning:** None yet.

head: Decision
What we chose
When
rows: Tools with no agreed fate

**File Sizes** goes live. **Travelling Salesperson, Route Inspection and Mixed Strategies** become part of a new prong, *Decision exam-style questions* (`docs/PROJECTS.md`), and go live through it. **Simplifying Ratios** is to be merged into a separate ratio tool after its Question Options are listed. **Perimeter** is to be reworked from a fresh brief
Slides

Slides moved out of the tidy-up list into the plan as their own prong (**Slides**, `docs/PROJECTS.md`): which of the four surfaces (Teach tab, lesson decks, the Depth stage, skill slides) survive is a build-out decision, not a loose end. Leaning kept there: keep Depth and the lesson decks; fold the Teach tab and skill slides into them
Printables

Named and wired into the shell: a tool passes `printables` and the burger menu lists them under one "Printables" heading, printed through one path (`src/shared/printables.ts`). Five shared sheets (number line, place value table, binary table, ratio table, coordinate grid) go on the tools whose working is built on that blank (the dashboard's Printables filter lists them); the rule is that a tool offers one only when students fill in a blank, and a test enforces it. The old one-off `menuItems` prop is gone. Bar-model strips were left out: no live tool uses the bar model yet
Registry ids

Every tool's id is its route without the slash, in lower-case words joined by hyphens (`ratio` → `ratio-sharing`, `integers` → `integer-add-and-subtract`, `Times Tables` → `times-tables` (its route moved from `/timestables`, which still redirects), `grapher-lab` → `grapher`, `system architecture` → `system-architecture`…: sixteen renamed). The ids are never in a link, so no route changed and no old link needed a redirect; the thing that carried an id was each tool's dashboard note, which was copied to the new id (the old entries stay in the store until the branch is merged, then are removed with the notes service's new `remove` action). A test (`src/tests/registryIds.test.ts`) fails on an id that is not kebab-case or not its route. The technique previews keep their `technique-preview-…` ids: they are pages, not tools
Strand homes

Binary & Number Bases is no longer its own strand: its five tools sit in Computer Science as the group "Binary & number bases", beside the group "Computer systems" (the revision topics). The Visualiser has a **Classroom** strand of its own and the internal pages (Tool Shell, Skill Library, Technique Library) a **Workshop** strand (Developing-tools mode only); both are `subject: 'All subjects'`, so they show on every subject tab. The folders (`src/tools/Binary/`, `src/tools/TeacherTools/`) stay where they are
Group label wording

Every Question Option group label (the heading over a pool or dropdown) is Title Case, and one word means one thing: **Method** (how it is worked: FOIL or grid, ratio table or decimal, digit rule or number line), **Working Shown** (how much working: full or constants only, long division or result only), **Answer Format** (how the answer is written), **Ask for** (what the question asks for), **Operation** (which operation). Sixty-odd labels changed; `src/tests/levelLabels.test.ts` fails on a label that is not Title Case or that goes back to a retired wording
Question Option labels

One vocabulary for the group labels (the heading over a pool or dropdown): a pool you can tick several of is plural ("Question Types", "Operations", "Bases", "Coefficients", "Solution Types"), one spelling per label across the site, and "Ask for" is the label for what a question asks for (never "Find" or "Ask"). 22 labels renamed; a test in `src/tests/levelLabels.test.ts` fails on a clash or a synonym
Question underscore fields

The data a tool hangs on a question for the shell (`_diagram`, `_rawValues`, `_stagedReveal`, `_stepFocus`, `_printText`…) is one interface, `QuestionExtras`, with a typed reader `extras(q)` and `withExtras(q, {…})` (`src/shared/questionExtras.ts`). Every read in the shell and the tools goes through it, so `as any` for these is gone (the shell's own reads of a question's fields are typed too, and the dead "frac" question kind was deleted from print, the worksheet view and the question display: `as any` casts in the app went from 111 to 13, three of them reading `window` and the rest in the standalone PDF generator, Rounding's cell drawing and one diagram helper). A test fails on any underscore field the interface does not list, on a listed one nothing uses, and on a new `(q as any)._x`. Writes are still object literals cast to `AnyQuestion`, checked by that name test; fields private to one tool are `unknown` in the interface and the tool narrows them where it reads
"About this tool"

One click-through panel from the burger menu, kept apart from the level (i) beside the level buttons (which stays). Its Question Options topic is written from the config; it opens once per live tool per device on the first visit (not from shared links or lessons), with "Show tool tips again" on the landing menu. Per-level teaching text is a later extra for the level (i)
Ordering a worksheet easy to hard

One mechanism: calibration. Eight tools score each question from the question itself and the worksheet spreads across eight bands: Order of Operations, Decimal Add/Sub, Speed Distance Time, File Sizes, Factor Theorem, Partial Fractions, Indices and Surds. Option weights are gone (`weight`, `weightOf`); `calibrated: true` marks a tool and a shared test kit checks it. Variety pools that should stay even on a short sheet are `balanced: true` (Rounding's zero kinds, Speed Distance Time's mixed types)
Hiding a tool

Two states only: live or not live (`enabled: false`, shown with Developing-tools mode). The `hidden` and `parked` switches and the separate parked gate (`?parked=1`) are gone. The dashboard and technique previews are `PAGES` in the registry (no state, no card). Skill drill-down links and the Skill Library now follow Developing-tools mode
Dev-mode working chains

Three tools (Simultaneous Equations, Non-linear Sim Eq, Fraction to Ratio) keep two versions of their working behind the developer switch. Decided to keep both for now and settle which a class sees inside each tool's own review: the question is already on each tool's dashboard note, so it no longer needs a card here
Printing diagrams

Basic Angle Facts and Angles in Parallel Lines now print through the shared `handleDiagramPrint` (their own print pages are gone; the parallel-lines answers keep their reasoning through a new `_printAnswer`, and both gain a choice of columns). Recipes keeps its own print on purpose: its "Needed / You Have" tables are not pictures
Colour scheme argument in the renderer API

The `colorScheme` argument is gone from every renderer (`questionRenderer`, `answerRenderer`, `stepRenderer`, `stepVisualRenderer`, the working scaffold's `render`) and from the worked-example steps. Positional arguments moved up by one, so the type-check found every tool that needed changing; `CLAUDE.md` shows the new signatures
Decision tools: story text separate from numbers
Not doing it now; a Decision option becomes display-only if and when a Decision tool is next reworked and the story text is separated then
Display-only options

Five more options now redraw the same question when flipped: Fractions "Whole & Part Method", Powers of 10 "10ⁿ notation", Percentages "Unitary method", Ratio Sharing "Numerical method" and Best Buys "Force unitary method" (it changes the comparison unit in the working and the answer line, never the packs; such a switch is marked `rewordsAnswer` and the test then checks the question is identical instead) (the other two on the old list, Decimal "Table starts" and the Geometry show-switches, already did). The existing test replays every flagged option and fails if the answer changes
Local copies of `randInt` / `pick`

The shared versions are used everywhere: the five tools and four Decision files that defined their own now import them (`pick` accepts read-only lists). Other helpers for `math.ts` (simplify fraction, prime factors, a `Fraction` type…) are added when a tool needs them, not ahead of time
File-local exports
148 exports that no other file used are no longer exported, and one dead function (`histHasNoHoles`) was deleted. A test (`src/tests/localExports.test.ts`) fails if a new one appears
Dashboard counts

The dashboard lists 79 tools of 80 registry entries; the one it leaves out is the dashboard itself, which is not a tool. A test (`src/tests/dashboardCounts.test.ts`) explains the gap and fails if another unlisted entry appears
Hook dependencies, everywhere

Every file under `src` now passes the React hooks lint rules, with no files left off the check. The last ones were fixed or justified: missing dependencies in `ExpandingBrackets`, `SystemArchitecture` and `ParallelLinesInteractive`; each deliberate exception in `SmartGrapher`, `DecisionShell`, `ExamView`, the CS `ExamMode`, `GrapherLab`, `WordsHangman` and `BinaryCounting` now says why. A test fails if one has no reason
Hook-dependency lint for the shell

ESLint with the React hooks rules is installed (`npm run lint`, run in CI beside the build and tests). The tool shell and the shared components pass it: each place that deliberately skips the rule says why (`-- deliberate: …`, enforced by a test), a missing dependency in the Escape-key, Visualiser and worked-example effects was fixed, and `npm run smoke:shell` also runs in CI in a real browser
The tool shell

Split from one 2,450-line file into a small lessons wrapper, a 990-line core, screen components (Whiteboard, Worked Example, Worksheet, phone layout) and small files for share links, options, worksheet generation and the question lifecycle. Every screen runs behind a guard that names it when it fails, generators fail without freezing the page, and failures are recorded with their setup. Tests and `npm run smoke:shell` check it
Where the level text lives
One (i) beside the level buttons on every tool, with a fuller pop-up per level; the Level entries left the burger menu
Changing a Question Option
It keeps the current question and the next one follows the new options; display-only options replay the same question instantly
Colour schemes
Removed from every tool; parked as a long-term accessibility idea
Recipes `\text{}` steps
Converted to `mStep` / `tStep`, and the smoke test now blocks them
Docs and code that disagreed
README, PROJECTS, CLAUDE, glossary, plans and spec statuses brought back in line with the code
Dev-mode working chains (Simultaneous Equations, Non-linear Sim Eq, Fraction to Ratio)
Keep both chains for now and settle per tool in its review

features.title: Modes — the tabs across the top of a tool

blocks.s: **For:** teaching from the front of the room. One question at a time, big, with a blank working space beside it (or the visualiser camera). **How it works:** New Question, Show Answer, text-size chevrons, fullscreen. **Where:** every tool.

**For:** showing how the answer is built, one mark at a time, so the class has thinking time. **How it works:** the step-by-step cascade reveals the working a line at a time (earlier steps stay on screen, dimmed); each line can itself build up in parts, in the order a teacher would write it on the board. Show All puts the whole working up at once. **Where:** every ToolShell tool.

**For:** a printable or on-screen set of practice questions. **How it works:** choose how many questions and columns, then Generate. Answers can be shown for the whole sheet or one cell at a time (double-tap a cell). Fullscreen fits the sheet to the screen. **Settings:** borders, Smart Progressor, say the prompt once, condensed wording. **Where:** every ToolShell tool.

**For:** one sheet with a column per level so a mixed-attainment class each gets their own. **How it works:** pick the levels; each column uses that level's own Question Options. **Where:** Worksheet mode, every ToolShell tool with more than one level.

**For:** going beyond generated practice: hand-written questions that find misconceptions, make students explain, and stretch the secure. **How it works:** the teacher dips in by purpose (diagnose, explain, extend) and level, in whatever order the class needs. Each item is a question slide then an answer slide, with cartoon speakers, lettered options that name the misconception behind each wrong choice, and Feathers the owl giving a nudge or takeaway. A "Start here" quick check gives one question per level. Items grey out when the Question Options needed for them are off. **Where:** the tools that have a question bank (see the Matrix).

**For:** the teaching part of a lesson, as slides pressed through one beat at a time before moving to practice. **How it works:** hand-written, misconception-driven slides with animated pictures (split bars, factor trees, index tiles). **Status:** Developing-tools mode only for now. **Where:** the tools with a deck (see the Matrix).

**For:** a teacher's sequence inside one tool: for example a Depth check, a Whiteboard practice, a Worksheet to set, then an extension. **How it works:** the burger menu's Lessons page shows a card per lesson; each step opens a pre-set mode, level and options, and a step bar keeps the place. **Status:** Developing-tools mode only for now.

**For:** ready-made sheets with no generated questions, for the class to fill in: blank number lines, place value tables, binary tables, ratio tables and coordinate grids. **How it works:** a "Printables" heading in the burger menu lists the sheets a tool offers; one click opens the A4 page ready to print. **Where:** only tools whose working is built on a blank the student fills in (a number line, place value table, ratio table or graph); the dashboard's Printables filter lists them.

features.title: Controls — what a teacher can change

blocks.s: **For:** moving the same question type from easy to harder. **How it works:** Level 1, 2 and 3 buttons above the question. A tool can offer fewer than three; the buttons it does not use are hidden. An (i) beside the buttons (on a phone, beside the Difficulty title) says what each level means; tapping a level opens a fuller pop-up with what can be chosen there and a button to switch to it. **Where:** every ToolShell tool, and the Decision tools.

**For:** tuning exactly what kind of questions come up (which question types, what sort of numbers, how the answer must be shown). **How it works:** a popover of buttons grouped into pools; ticking more than one in a pool mixes them. A label ending in an asterisk is beyond standard questioning and is off by default. Some options grey out until another option they depend on is on. Every option says in a sentence what it is for (hover its (i) on a laptop; on the Decision tools the sentence shows beside the option's heading, or under it on a phone or tablet), and the headings use one wording across the site: Title Case, one word per idea ("Method" is how it is worked, "Working Shown" is how much working, "Answer Format" is how the answer is written, "Ask for" is what the question asks for). **Where:** every tool.

**For:** telling the teacher in plain words what the tool is for. **How it works:** opened from the burger menu ("About this tool"); it says what the whole tool is for, then lists each sub-tool with its purpose; a sub-tool opens to show what each of its levels means and what its Question Options do (each one explained in a sentence, such as what 'Extended Range' extends; the same note appears when you hover an option's ⓘ). The level text is the same as in the level (i), which gives the quick version for the tab you are on. It does not explain the modes. It opens by itself the first time a live tool is used on a device (never from a shared link or a lesson step) and then stays out of the way; "Show tool tips again" on the landing page menu brings that back. On a phone it is a full-screen sheet. **Where:** every ToolShell, Decision and Computer Science tool, the word games, the Visualiser and the Parallel Lines Explorer (these last ones keep hand-written notes). Each ToolShell tool also has a level (i) beside the level buttons: it says what Level 1, 2 and 3 mean, and tapping a level opens a fuller pop-up with what can be chosen at that level and a button to switch to it.

**For:** several related question types in one tool (for example Elimination and Substitution). **How it works:** small tabs under the title; a tool with only one sub-tool shows none. **Where:** most ToolShell tools.

**For:** sending a colleague or a class the exact setup: mode, level, options, question count. **How it works:** the address bar always holds the current setup; the burger menu copies it. A worksheet link generates the sheet on arrival. Old links never break, and when a tool's address changes the old address still opens it (Times Tables moved from `/timestables` to `/times-tables`). **Where:** every ToolShell tool.

**For:** going back to a question the class has moved on from, or keeping one on hand. **How it works:** the burger menu lists the last five questions and up to five pinned ones; the pin button sits beside New Question. Memory only: gone when the page reloads. **Where:** both shells.

features.title: Subjects and strands on the landing page

blocks.s: **For:** finding a tool by subject. **How it works:** three tabs, GCSE Maths, A-Level and Computer Science, each listing its strands in order of the scheme of work. Computer Science holds the revision topics ("Computer systems") and the binary and number-base generators ("Binary & number bases") together. The Classroom strand (the Visualiser) shows under every tab; internal pages sit in a Workshop strand that appears only in Developing-tools mode. **Where:** landing page.

**For:** previewing the phone or tablet layout, or fixing a device that guesses wrong. **How it works:** a landing-page menu setting, stored per device, that every shell obeys. **Where:** landing page burger menu.

**For:** writing on top of any tool page, on a touch screen or interactive whiteboard. **How it works:** a pencil button opens a movable bar with Freeze, Pen, Eraser, Undo, Clear and colours. Ink stays until you change page. **Where:** every tool page, not the landing page.

features.title: Fullscreen and the collapsible working panel

blocks.s: **For:** filling the screen for a whole-class view. **How it works:** Fullscreen enlarges the question; the working or visualiser panel on the right can be collapsed so a large diagram fills the width, and re-opened from a button in the question box. **Where:** Whiteboard.
**For:** showing a student's paper or a hand-drawn working alongside the question. **How it works:** the working panel can show the live camera. **Where:** Whiteboard and the Visualiser tool.

**For:** a model for the students to copy while they work, such as a place value table. **How it works:** drawn in the working box or beside the question, with a button to hide it once students no longer need it. **Where:** the tools that have one (see the Matrix).

**For:** letting the class attempt part of the task before the answer, such as plotting a number before the answer line appears. **How it works:** an extra button in the question box (for example "Show Plot") reveals the in-between picture; Show Answer still shows everything. **Where:** Rounding.

features.title: On the worksheet — how a sheet is built

blocks.s: **For:** putting a worksheet in order from easy to hard by how hard each question really is, not by which option made it. **How it works:** each question is scored from its own numbers and working; a sample of thousands cuts the scores into eight bands, and the sheet draws evenly from the bands the ticked options can reach, easy first. A **Smart Progressor** switch in Worksheet Settings turns it off. A few variety pools (the zero kinds in Rounding, Speed / Distance / Time in a mix) are also kept roughly even on a short sheet by the same switch. **Where:** every tool with the Calibrated mark on the dashboard.

**For:** a cleaner sheet when every question starts with the same instruction ("Simplify:"). **How it works:** the shared wording is shown once above the sheet instead of in every cell. Printing still repeats it. A switch in Settings puts it back.

**For:** fitting more questions on a sheet by shortening long wording. **How it works:** a switch in Worksheet Settings shows the question with a small tag ("(3 d.p.)") instead of the full sentence. Print and the whiteboard keep the full wording.

features.title: Answers in place of the question

blocks.s: **For:** checking a sheet cell by cell. **How it works:** with answers on, each cell shows its answer instead of the question; double-tap a cell to flip just that one.

**For:** printing sheets of pictures (angles, number lines, grids) neatly, with the right number per page. **How it works:** diagrams are packed by their shape using the same page-fill engine as text sheets; more columns means smaller, denser diagrams. **Where:** the diagram tools.

features.title: Behind the scenes — what makes a question good

blocks.s: **For:** changing how a question is shown without changing the question. **How it works:** when a display option is switched (decimal or fraction, say, or words in the column headings), the shell redraws the same maths in the new form instead of making a new question, so the class keeps the problem they were looking at. Every tool gets this for any option marked as display-only. **Where:** every tool, for its display options.

**For:** changing your mind without losing the question on screen. **How it works:** changing a Question Option no longer replaces the current question. The next question you ask for follows the new options. Only a change of level or sub-tool gives a new question straight away. **Where:** Whiteboard and Worked Example in every tool, and the Decision tools.

**For:** a Worked Example where one picture is drawn up step by step beside the working (a place value table filling in, a graph being built, a diagram getting its angles). **How it works:** the picture updates in place as the steps advance instead of being reprinted each time. **Where:** the tools marked on the Matrix.

**For:** the working ending by stating the answer, so no separate answer box is needed. **How it works:** a tool whose last step already states the exact answer can switch the extra green answer box off.

**For:** the same picture meaning the same thing wherever a student meets it. **How it works:** bar model, number line, area model, algebra tiles, negative counters, prime factor tiles, place value table and ratio table are the site's visual vocabulary; new pictures must start from one of them. The Matrix shows which tool uses which.

**For:** reusable blocks of worked-example steps (solving a linear equation, substituting back) so many tools explain the same move the same way. **Status:** built and used by a few tools; a Technique Library page shows them in Developing-tools mode.

**For:** a dotted-underline word in the working (for example "LCM") that would open a short slide lesson on that skill. **Status:** Developing-tools mode only: the markers are in three tools and show as plain text otherwise.

**For:** catching a broken question before a teacher meets it. **How it works:** every tool is run through 40 questions per tab and level; the tests fail on a crash, a repeated question key or any maths that will not draw. The Matrix shows which tools are covered.
**For:** a written brief in `specs/` that says what a tool should teach, with sample questions that define "correct". The Matrix shows which tools have one.
